question.problem:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the following probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12}(2-x), & -3<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

If the probability density function of $Y={X}^{2}$ is given by 

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}g(y), & 0<y<1 \\ h(y), & 1\le y<9 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

find the function $g(y).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's visualize the transformation $Y={X}^{2}$ over the interval $-3<x<1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14231916/assets/7332c58097d1a2933c10152028bc715a147e820ae14b2fae92fe288eaf956ce0.png)

Notice the following:

- The transformation is one-to-one over the interval $-3<x\le -1.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $1\le y<9.$

- The transformation is two-to-one over the interval $-1<x<1.$ On this interval, $Y$ is nonzero on $0<y<1.$

In this question, we're asked to consider only the interval $0<y<1.$ 

Using the definition of the cumulative distribution of $Y,$ for $0<y<1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =P(Y\le y) \\  & =P({X}^{2}\le y) \\  & =P(-\sqrt{y}\le X\le \sqrt{y}) \\  & ={F}_{X}(\sqrt{y})-{F}_{X}(-\sqrt{y}).\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the PDF ${f}_{Y}(y)$ for $0<y<1,$ we differentiate ${F}_{Y}$ with respect to $y$ using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={F}_{Y}^{′}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}(\sqrt{y})+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}(-\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(\sqrt{y})+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot {f}_{X}(-\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}({f}_{X}(\sqrt{y})+{f}_{X}(-\sqrt{y})).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the definition of ${f}_{X},$ we finally arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}({f}_{X}(\sqrt{y})+{f}_{X}(-\sqrt{y})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}(\frac{1}{12}(2-\sqrt{y})+\frac{1}{12}(2+\sqrt{y})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $g(y)=\frac{1}{6\sqrt{y}}.$
